sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Cosmological Constant (Λ)**: Introduced by Einstein, it represents the energy density of empty space; it is the simplest explanation for Dark Energy.
• **Accelerated Expansion**: Observed in 1998 via Type Ia Supernovae, proving the universe is not just expanding, but speeding up.
• **Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)**: Fluctuations in the CMB radiation provide a 'snapshot' of the early universe, confirming the flat geometry of space requiring Dark Energy.
• **Key Metric**: The **Equation of State parameter (w)**, where w = -1 for a perfect cosmological constant.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Dark Energy Survey (DES)**: An international collaboration using ground-based telescopes to map the large-scale structure of the universe.
• **Roman Space Telescope**: NASA's upcoming mission to perform a high-precision survey of the expansion history.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The 'Hubble Tension'—a discrepancy between expansion rates measured via CMB vs. local distance ladders.
• **Solutions**: Next-gen gravitational wave astronomy and high-precision spectroscopic surveys.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-B-C' (Supernovae, BAO, CMB).
• **Decoded Meaning**: The three pillars of Dark Energy evidence: Supernovae (Standard Candles), BAO (Standard Rulers), and CMB (Early Universe Snapshot).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Dark Energy is NOT the same as Dark Matter. Dark Matter acts as 'cosmic glue' (attractive gravity), while Dark Energy acts as 'cosmic expander' (repulsive pressure).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Cosmic Acceleration' to describe the current epoch of the universe, distinguishing it from the 'Deceleration' phase dominated by matter.

keyTakeaways: Dark Energy accounts for ~68% of the universe's energy density.
Evidence is derived from Type Ia Supernovae, BAO, and CMB data.
The Hubble Tension remains the most significant unsolved problem in modern cosmology.
